title: Reviewer findings say whether they block approval, and every task gets a review round budget that stops for the captain
public_title: Tag review findings by severity and cap review rounds
acceptance: Why. Today a code review can run for many rounds over one finding, because nothing tells the reviewer when a change is good enough and nothing stops the loop. A finding on the standing list (the numbered list that every rejecting review ends with, closed by `CRITERIA-COMPLETE:<task-id>`; design/design.md section 7) is either open or done, and every open finding blocks approval the same way. Example: in the task that bounds SSH transfers (T-262), item 4 was added in review round 3 and was still marked `open` in rounds 4, 5, 6 and 7, with the reviewer chasing Git configuration edge cases, until the captain stopped it by hand. Operator-retained private receipts in the firstmate-workflow evidence store for that task, given as round, first 12 characters of the reviewed head and first 12 characters of the record signature: round 3 `78fa300ab061` `07291a1705cd`; round 4 `6089aa89976f` `ed8ad21b3e0e`; round 5 `fea4409b617a` `ba21a64980f5`; round 6 `3f2145373418` `3e3efbae88ab`; round 7 `32b2291b924d` `cf7aad24d5f9`. These are references for the motive only; no test depends on them.

How, in one paragraph. This task adds two things. First, each finding carries a severity tag: `[must-fix]` blocks approval, `[follow-up]` is recorded but does not block, and the reviewer may approve while follow-ups stay open; firstmate then proposes those follow-ups as new tasks on a captain card. Second, each task gets a review round budget (default 3 review rounds, set in config.yaml). When a rejection uses up the budget, or when the same must-fix item stays open in 2 consecutive review rounds, the autopilot (the background service `bin/fm-autopilot.sh` that gates pull requests, launches reviews and wakes firstmate) stops the task and raises a captain card with three choices: narrow the scope, park the task, or continue for a few more rounds. The card shows the round history.

Terms. A 'review round' is one round number among the task's retained reviewer verdict records (kind `verdict`, read through `Store.verdicts()` in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, so the existing FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN filter applies). When several records share a round number, the round is represented by the last of them in retention order (the order `Store.records()` returns); that record alone gives the round's verdict and standing list for the stop rule and the card history. Rounds are ordered by round number. An 'open item' follows the same definition as the fix-proposal task this one depends on (T-272): in the task's first standing list, any item whose first line does not start with `done` (optionally bold); in a later list, an item whose first line starts with `open` (optionally bold), or a new item labelled `REGRESSION:<task-id>` or `NEW-GROUND:<task-id>`. A 'marked' verdict is one that carries the new field `severity_protocol: 1` (see Migration).

Order with the fix-proposal task. This task depends on T-272 (pull request #261, a rejecting reviewer attaches a concrete fix to every open finding) and is dispatched only after that pull request has merged. Both tasks change the same places: the standing-list rules in skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, protocol() in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, the review prompt in bin/fm-review.sh and the two REJECT branches in bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py. Building second lets this task extend T-272's code instead of both tasks rewriting the same lines. T-272's rules stay as they are: every open item, a follow-up included, still carries one fix proposal or one `DECISION:` line.

Change 1, the tag format. The severity tag is the text `[must-fix]` or `[follow-up]` on the first line of a standing-list item, anywhere on that line, for example `2. open [follow-up]: rename the helper` or `3. REGRESSION:T-9 [must-fix] the lock is never released`. An item whose first line has no tag is must-fix. This rule applies to every record, old or new, so all items written before this task count as must-fix.

Change 1, parsing. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py gains a function `severity(body)` that returns `must-fix` or `follow-up` for one item body as criteria() returns it. A first line that holds both tags is reported by protocol() as `item <N> has two severity tags` for a marked record. criteria() itself does not change, so its existing caller, the worker context pack (bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py around line 329), still receives the full item text, tag included, and needs no change.

Change 1, rejecting needs a must-fix item. For a marked REJECT, protocol() reports `REJECT has no open must-fix item` when no open item in its standing list is must-fix. A review whose open items are all follow-ups must be an APPROVE.

Change 1, approving with follow-ups. For a marked APPROVE that carries its own standing list, protocol() reports `APPROVE leaves must-fix item <N> open` for each open must-fix item in that list. Open follow-up items do not cause an error. A marked APPROVE without its own list stays valid, as an ordinary approval is today.

Change 1, gate 6. Gate 6 (the approval gate, `fm_evidence.py gate`, called from bin/fm-gate.sh around line 270) already runs protocol() over the task's verdicts, so it refuses a marked APPROVE that leaves a must-fix item open, with the protocol message above. No other gate changes.

Change 1, the autopilot checks a marked APPROVE before the gate. Today advance() in bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py (around line 473) runs the protocol check only from round 3 and otherwise runs the gate, and a gate 6 failure launches another review. When the task's latest verdict is a marked APPROVE for the pull request's current head, advance() runs the protocol check (`bin/fm-protocol.sh check`) first, in every round. On failure the existing protocol-violation wake is raised and no review is launched for that head. On success the gate runs as today.

Change 1, the reviewer rule. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, section 'Every REJECT closes its list', gains the tag rule: tag every item `[must-fix]` or `[follow-up]`; must-fix means this head cannot merge without it; follow-up means the change is correct without it and the item is worth a separate task; keep an item's tag across rounds unless the reasoning changed, and say why when it changes; reject only when at least one must-fix item is open; approve when every open item is a follow-up, re-issuing the list so the follow-ups are recorded. The reviewer prompt includes this file in every round (bin/fm-review.sh around line 870), round one included.

Change 1, the review prompt. The closing sentence that closed_list() prints from round 2 (bin/fm-review.sh around line 582) gains: keep each item's `[must-fix]` or `[follow-up]` tag, and an untagged item counts as must-fix. Its other sentences stay as they are.

Change 1, the worker's brief draft. T-272's `fixes-brief` command (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py) writes an open follow-up item as `<N>. deferred: follow-up, not needed for approval: <first line of the item>` instead of a `fix:` line, so the next worker round fixes must-fix items first. Its fix proposal is still copied below that line. The coverage check in bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py accepts `deferred:` lines today, so that file does not change.

Change 1, follow-ups become proposed tasks. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py gains a command `follow-ups --task <id>` that prints, as JSON, the open follow-up items (number and first line) of the task's latest verdict when it is an APPROVE: from that APPROVE's own list, or, when it has none, from the latest earlier list. When the latest verdict is a marked APPROVE for the current head and that list is not empty, advance() queues one wake per head, `<task> approved with <n> open follow-ups; propose follow-up tasks on a card` in English and `<task> 已核准，但仍有 <n> 個後續項目；請在決策卡上提出後續任務` in Traditional Chinese. The follow-ups never hold the merge card.

Change 1, firstmate's rule. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, section 'Operate the shipped loop', says: on the follow-ups wake, read `follow-ups`, group the items into proposed tasks and raise one choice card with `--purpose decision` that lists them; nothing is dispatched until the captain answers, as for every other proposal.

Change 2, configuration. config.yaml gains a top-level block `review_budget:` with keys `rounds: 3` (review rounds before the captain decides), `stall: 2` (consecutive review rounds a must-fix item may stay open) and `extend: 2` (rounds added by a 'continue' answer), each with a one-line comment. A new module bin/lib/fm_round_budget.py reads them with the one config reader, `fm_cfg_in review_budget <key> <file>` in bin/fm-config.sh, always naming the file explicitly: the engine checkout's own config.yaml (the autopilot passes `<engine root>/config.yaml`, the root it already holds as `self.root`; bin/fm-worker.sh passes `"$REPO/config.yaml"`), the same file bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py around line 195 reads for `concurrency`. External projects use that engine file; there is no per-project budget. A frozen launcher reads the engine file at the moment it runs. A missing block or key uses the default. A value that is not a whole number from 1 to 99 is an error that names the key. A test sets the same non-default values once and proves the autopilot and the worker check both read them.

Change 2, when a task stops. bin/lib/fm_round_budget.py decides the task's budget state from the evidence store, the config and the budget cards (below). The task stops when its latest round is a marked REJECT and either the number of review rounds is at least the current budget, or one item number is open and must-fix in the standing lists of `stall` consecutive review rounds. A streak counts rounds in round-number order; a round whose representative record is an APPROVE, has no standing list, or holds that item as done or as a follow-up breaks the streak for that item. Earlier unmarked rounds count in the streak and in the round count, parsed the same way (untagged items are must-fix); only the latest round must be marked. Only rounds after the round of the latest budget card count toward `stall`. With the defaults, the third rejecting review round stops the task, and an item still open in the round after the one that raised it stops the task.

Change 2, the budget card record. Each budget card is recorded in `<project state>/round-budget/<task>.json`, where <project state> is the state directory the evidence Store already uses (self: state/; external: the private project state). The file holds a version and a list of cards, each with the card id, the head and verdict signature that stopped the task, that verdict's round, the round count and budget at that moment, the `extend` value, the task's current spec pin version at that moment (read through the existing resolver in bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py, or null when the task has no pin) and the time it was raised. It is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) under a lock file in the same directory. `fm_round_budget.py record-card --task <id> --id <decision id>` records a card for the task's latest stopping verdict and refuses a second card for the same verdict signature, except in the pinless case described below. A card's answer is the answered decision record `<project state>/decisions/<id>.json` whose `id` equals the recorded id and whose `task` equals the task; its `chosen` is A, B or C and its `ts` is the answer time. A record whose id or task does not match is ignored.

Change 2, the autopilot stops the task. In both REJECT branches of bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py (advance() near line 392 and job_completed() near line 618), after T-272's protocol check passes and before T-272's review-fixes or 'brief needed' wake, the autopilot asks bin/lib/fm_round_budget.py for the state. When the task stops, it raises no review-fixes wake, no 'brief needed' wake and no review, and goes on to the card step below. When the state is 'within budget' or a 'continue' answer covers it, both branches behave exactly as after T-272.

Change 2, jobs already running when a task stops or is held. job_completed() in bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py, after its existing landed check, asks for the budget state for gate, protocol and review results. When the task is stopped, parked or waiting for a narrowed repin, a protocol success starts no gate, a gate exit 6 launches no review, a gate exit 0 raises no merge card, and a review result follows only the budget path above; the job is still marked done. After a restart, recover_jobs() replays results through the same function, so the hold applies there too. A test runs each of these results for a held task and proves no gate, review or merge card starts.

Change 2, the card for the self project. For the self project the autopilot builds the card details from the round history into `<project state>/decision-details-built/<id>.json`, allocates an id with `bin/fm-decide.sh --allocate --task <task> --project <project>`, records it with record-card, and requests it with `bin/fm-decide.sh --request <id> --task <task> --project <project> --purpose decision --details <file>`. After a restart, a recorded card with no pending or answered file is requested again with the same id. If the build or the request fails, the autopilot queues one wake per verdict, `<task>: round budget card failed: <reason>; raise it by hand and run record-card` in English and `<task>：回合預算決策卡建立失敗：<原因>；請手動提出並執行 record-card` in Traditional Chinese.

Change 2, the card content. The built details are a choice card in English and Traditional Chinese with: a title saying the task's review rounds ran out and the captain chooses the next step; one fact per review round (round number, the first 12 characters of the head, the verdict, and the open must-fix and open follow-up item numbers, at most 5 numbers each followed by 'and <k> more'), at most 10 rounds, with older rounds summarised in one fact; one fact naming the items that stayed open for `stall` rounds, at most 5 numbers; and options A 'Narrow the scope', B 'Park the task' and C 'Continue <extend> more review rounds', each with a description, a benefit and a cost. Every fact stays within the word limits of bin/lib/fm_ste.py (25 English words, 30 Chinese units) and the string limits fm-decide.sh applies to details. The full history stays available in private state through `fm_round_budget.py history --task <id>`. The details pass `bin/lib/fm_ste.py check-details --kind choice` with no failing rule. A test with 30 open items in each of 12 rounds passes the details check and a real `fm-decide.sh --request` in a test state.

Change 2, the wake. When a card is requested or recorded, the autopilot queues one wake per card, `<task>: round budget reached (<rounds> of <budget> review rounds); captain card <id>` in English and `<task>：審查回合已達上限（<rounds>／<budget>）；決策卡 <id>` in Traditional Chinese. Wakes go through the existing queue; no new event type is added, so bin/fm-diagram.sh and bin/fm-emit.sh do not change.

Change 2, answer C, continue. When the latest budget card is answered C, the budget becomes that card's round count plus `extend`, the `stall` count restarts after that card's round, and the autopilot raises the normal wake for the stopping REJECT (T-272's review-fixes wake or 'brief needed', same text) under a card-specific identity, `budget-continue-<card id>`, so an earlier wake for the same head cannot suppress it and a restart cannot repeat it. A test queues the ordinary REJECT wake for the head first, then answers C, and proves exactly one continue wake follows, also after a restart.

Change 2, answer B, park. When the latest budget card is answered B, advance() returns for that task's pull request before any gate, review or REJECT wake, after queueing once per card `<task> parked by the captain (card <id>)` in English and `<task> 已由船長暫停（決策卡 <id>）` in Traditional Chinese. Nothing is written to GitHub; the pull request stays open.

Change 2, answer A, narrow the scope. When the latest budget card is answered A, the autopilot queues once per card `<task>: captain chose to narrow the scope (card <id>); prepare a repin` in English and `<task>：船長選擇縮小範圍（決策卡 <id>）；請準備重新釘選規格` in Traditional Chinese, and holds the task like a park until it is repinned.

Change 2, leaving park or narrow. A task held by an A or B answer is released only when the task's current spec pin, read through the existing resolver in bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py, meets three conditions: its version is greater than the pin version recorded on the card; its source is `repin`; and its captain approval time, which the resolver already verifies against the captain's `decision_made` event (`spec_approval.time` when that field is present, otherwise `approval.time`), is later than the budget answer's `ts`. Its exact spec bytes must also have a SPEC-OK spec-preflight record. That is the existing repin path: a captain repin card, `bin/fm-project.sh repin`, and an exact-byte preflight. A preflighted candidate that was never pinned, a SPEC-OK for the same bytes as before, and a repin whose captain approval came before the budget answer (even if the pin was written after it) do not release the task. On release the budget becomes the card's round count plus `rounds`, and `stall` restarts after the card's round. bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py does not change, and the pin format gains no field.

Change 2, a task with no pin. A task reviewed without any spec pin (a task dispatched before pins existed) records a null pin version on its card. Because a repin needs an existing pin (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py around line 453) and the worker launcher refuses a held task before it would create a first pin, such a task cannot be released by a repin. For it, an A or B hold ends only through a new budget card that the captain answers C: record-card accepts a second card for the same stopping verdict only when the task has no pin and the previous card for that verdict is answered A or B. firstmate raises that card when the captain asks to resume. Tests cover an A hold and a B hold on a pinless task: neither is released by a SPEC-OK alone, and each is released by a later card answered C.

Change 2, the worker launcher refuses. bin/fm-worker.sh runs `python3 "${FM_CODE_ROOT:-$REPO}/bin/lib/fm_round_budget.py" check --state "$FM_STATE_DIR" --project "$(fm_evidence_project)" --task "$TASK" --config "$REPO/config.yaml"` right after the early `fm_pin preflight` call (around line 77), before `fm_identity worker` allocates a round (around line 89). The check exits 65 with a message naming the card id, or saying no card was raised yet, when the task is stopped, parked or waiting for a narrowed repin; the launcher then exits 65. Otherwise it exits 0 and prints nothing. A configuration error also exits 65. A test proves that a refused launch writes no identity, emits no round event, creates no worktree change and starts no vendor.

Change 2, firstmate's rule. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, section 'Operate the shipped loop', lists the round-budget, park, narrow and card-failed wakes; says that firstmate does not brief or dispatch a stopped task; and says that for answer A firstmate writes a smaller spec, preflights it and raises the usual repin card.

Migration. retain_verdict in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py writes `severity_protocol: 1` on every verdict it retains after this change. The rules of Change 1 that can fail a record (two tags, REJECT without a must-fix item, APPROVE leaving a must-fix item open) apply only to marked records. The stop rule of Change 2 fires only on a marked REJECT, while the round count includes every earlier review round. So a task in flight with 3 or more rounds stops at its next rejection under the new launcher, not at a rejection retained before. A review round still running on an old frozen launcher retains its verdict without the field and is judged by today's rules. Existing pins, briefs, verdict bytes, signatures and decision records are not rewritten. Tests cover each of these cases, including an existing unmarked REJECT at round 5 that keeps today's 'brief needed' wake and no card.

External privacy. For an external project the autopilot does not build card details: it queues `<task>: round budget reached (<rounds> of <budget> review rounds); author the round budget card` in English and `<task>：審查回合已達上限（<rounds>／<budget>）；請撰寫回合預算決策卡` in Traditional Chinese, and firstmate raises the card and runs record-card. The card-failed wake for an external project omits the reason. The round-budget file and the round history stay in the private project state. No wake, event summary or other public output carries item text, a head, a reviewer name, a failure reason or a private path, including wakes queued again after a restart. A test under `FM_EXTERNAL=1` proves this, and proves that two projects with the same task id keep separate round-budget files.

Callers and fixtures. The worker sweeps with grep and keeps every caller working: criteria() (bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py:329, unchanged; parser tests in tests/lib/standing_list.py); protocol() through `fm_evidence.py gate` and `protocol` (bin/fm-gate.sh:270, bin/fm-protocol.sh:43, tests/protocol.test.sh) and tests/lib/review_experiment_evidence.py:1001, which asserts no errors for unmarked records and stays as it is; retain_verdict() through tests/lib/evidence_binding.py:42, tests/lib/local_round_records.py and tests/local-round-loop.test.sh, whose untagged items are must-fix and so stay valid; advance() and job_completed() tests in tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py, which build verdicts without the new field and so keep today's behaviour, including test_reject_wakes_once_without_worker_or_review. That file holds 1200 lines and must not grow, so new autopilot cases go in tests/lib/round_budget.py. tests/lib/worker.sh, tests/lib/review.sh and tests/crew-end-to-end.test.sh copy the whole bin/lib, so they receive the new module without change. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py imports bin/lib/fm_round_budget.py nowhere, so sparse evidence consumers stay independent of it.

i18n and lint. No key is added to i18n/ui.en.json or i18n/ui.zh-TW.json; the purpose `decision` and its badge already exist. Every wake and card in this task carries its own English and Traditional Chinese text. The board derives Simplified Chinese from Traditional through i18n/tw2cn.tsv; the worker adds an entry there for any word of the fixed card or wake text that the table does not yet convert, and a test converts each fixed string with that table and compares it with an expected Simplified Chinese string. New shell lines pass the existing lints in bin/ci.sh.

Design. design/design.md section 7 (The standing list) gains, at its end and before section 8, paragraphs on the severity tags, the three new protocol errors (two tags on one item, a REJECT with no open must-fix item, an APPROVE leaving a must-fix item open), gate 6's handling of a marked APPROVE, the follow-up wake, the round budget with its configuration, the stop rule, the card and its three answers, and the migration. No other section changes.

Tests, new behaviour that fails on the current main for a behavioural reason (name each assertion in .fm-say.md): a marked APPROVE whose own list leaves a must-fix item open fails `fm_evidence.py gate` and `protocol` (main accepts it); a marked REJECT whose open items are all follow-ups fails `protocol` (main accepts it); a first line with both tags fails `protocol` for a marked record; advance() runs the protocol check before the gate for a marked APPROVE in round 1 (main runs the gate); the third marked REJECT, with a different item open in each round so the stall rule cannot fire, raises a budget card and no 'brief needed' wake (main wakes for a brief); with `rounds: 5` and the same distinct-item history the stop moves to round 5; a must-fix item open in two consecutive marked REJECTs in rounds 1 and 2 raises the card; an answer C raises exactly one continue wake and moves the next stop to the card's round count plus `extend`; an answer B stops gates, reviews and REJECT wakes for that pull request; a held task's running protocol, gate and review results start no gate, review or merge card; an answer A holds the task until an authorized repin with a new SPEC-OK is pinned after the answer; bin/fm-worker.sh exits 65 for a stopped task and creates no round identity (main starts the round); a marked APPROVE with open follow-ups queues one follow-ups wake per head in both languages.

Tests, new interface (absent on main, not counted as fail-first evidence): severity() cases (untagged, each tag, tag after a state word, after a REGRESSION label, inside a bold state); the `follow-ups` command with and without the APPROVE's own list; T-272's fixes-brief writing a `deferred: follow-up` line and still passing the coverage check in bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py; fm_round_budget.py state results; a round with two verdict records where the later one decides, also with FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN set; stall streaks broken by an APPROVE round, a no-list round, a done item and an item changed to follow-up, and a streak across an unmarked and a marked round; record-card refusal of a second card for one verdict; answer matching that ignores a decision record with another id or task; release of a B hold by a later authorized repin; no release by an unpinned preflighted candidate, by a SPEC-OK for the same bytes, or by a repin whose captain approval time is before the answer even when the pin file was written after it; atomic writes; configuration defaults, the error for an invalid value and both consumers reading the same file; a task with no verdicts passing `fm_round_budget.py check` silently; built card details with 30 open items in 12 rounds passing `fm_ste.py check-details --kind choice` and a real request; restart of the card step requesting the same id; the card-failed wake; external privacy, including failure and restart wakes; the tw2cn conversion of the fixed text. New files: tests/review-severity.test.sh, tests/lib/review_severity.py, tests/round-budget.test.sh and tests/lib/round_budget.py.

Tests, compatibility that passes on main and must keep passing: an unmarked APPROVE with open items still passes protocol (tests/protocol.test.sh around line 83); an unmarked REJECT at round 5 gives the 'brief needed' wake and no card (tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py around line 212); a marked APPROVE whose list has only open follow-ups passes protocol and the gate's protocol step; a worker launch for a task with no verdicts behaves as on main through the existing worker launcher fixtures (tests/lib/worker.sh); the existing autopilot, protocol, gate, standing-list and review-evidence suites stay green without edits.

Overlap. Pull request #260 (T-270, plain writing) also edits skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, bin/fm-review.sh, bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py, bin/lib/fm_ste.py and i18n/tw2cn.tsv, and adds required card sections; whichever merges second rebases, keeps both rule sets, and, if this task is second, fills those sections in the built budget card so it still passes the card checks. Pull request #261 (T-272) is a dependency, see the ordering line. Pull request #259 (T-271, live round view) shares only skills/firstmate/SKILL.md and design/design.md, in other sections. The retrospective task (T-273, being specified) also edits config.yaml, skills/firstmate/SKILL.md and design/design.md, in other blocks and sections. The flaky-test root-cause task (T-274, being specified) shares no file known today. Pull requests #257 (T-260) and #248 (T-262) also edit bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py, and T-262 also edits bin/fm-worker.sh and bin/fm-review.sh; this task rebases onto whatever has merged.

Unchanged. The standing-list numbering, done and open states, REGRESSION and NEW-GROUND labels, the CRITERIA-COMPLETE, APPROVE and REJECT markers, the ASK-PASS-CRITERIA exception, T-272's fix-proposal and two-reviewer rules, the FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN filter, spec preflight and its own standing list, merge cards, and the board. A reviewer can still change an item's tag between rounds; the protocol does not police that, and the card shows each round's open must-fix and follow-up numbers so the captain can see it.
